newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end softer, but golds restrain fall.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end softer, but golds restrain fall.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended softer on Friday, but strength in key sectors helped the Canadian market avoid New York's steep decline.
The TSE 300 Composite Index slipped 6.93 points to close at 6033.58 in heavy turnover of 102.55 million shares worth C$1.73 billion ($1.3 billion).
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average extended Thursday's sharp losses with a 59-point decline on Friday.

"We're getting some profit taking in those groups that have moved recently. It may continue next week, but I wouldn't consider this the beginning of something major," said Ron Meisels, president of P and C Holdings Ltd. in Montreal.
Toronto's nine weak sectors included consumer products, forestry, communications and pipelines. They were offset by precious metals and conglomerates, which led five groups aloft.

"We haven't completed it (the correction) yet. But at the same time, we're likely to see support at around 5950," Meisels said. In today's action, declining stocks outstripped advances 518 to 442, with 291 issues unchanged.
* Kasten Chase Applied Research Ltd topped actives, rising 0.15 to 4.10 on 3.17 million shares.
The communications firm announced plans on Friday for a C$11.25 million ($8.4 million) warrant issue to complete the financing of its merger with Disys Corp.
* TimberWest Forest Ltd. jumped 1 to 18.75 on 1.2 million shares after the lumber producer announced higher earnings and a decision to sell its privately-owned timberlands.
* Among gold shares, Barrick Gold Corp. gained 0.80 to 36.20, while Placer Dome Inc. rose 0.60 to 27.50. Gold stocks were helped by higher Comex precious metal futures on Friday.
* Entertainment giant Seagram Co. Ltd. sank 1.15 to 52.85 on 573,000 shares, dragging down the consumer products group.
